# 1 Chronicles Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 380r–380v

---

**1** Some time later, David attacked the Philistines and brought them under his control. He captured Gath and its surrounding towns from Philistine hands.

**2** He also defeated Moab. The Moabites became David's subjects and paid him tribute.

**3** David struck down Hadadezer king of Zobah near Hamath, as Hadadezer was marching to extend his power to the Euphrates River.

**4** David captured a thousand of his chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He crippled all the chariot horses, keeping only enough for a hundred chariots.

**5** When the Arameans from Damascus came to reinforce Hadadezer king of Zobah, David cut down twenty-two thousand of them.

**6** David stationed garrisons in Aramean Damascus, and the Arameans became his subjects and paid tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

**7** David seized the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's officers and brought them to Jerusalem.

**8** From Tibhath and Cun, cities belonging to Hadadezer, David carried off a huge quantity of bronze — the same bronze that Solomon would later use to make the great bronze basin, the pillars, and the bronze furnishings for the temple.

**9** When Tou king of Hamath learned that David had crushed the entire army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

**10** he sent his son Hadoram to King David to congratulate him on his victory over Hadadezer, who had been Tou's enemy. Hadoram brought with him gifts of gold, silver, and bronze.

**11** King David dedicated all of these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had plundered from every nation he conquered — Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.

**12** Abishai son of Zeruiah defeated eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

**13** He stationed garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites became David's subjects. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

**14** David ruled over all Israel. He governed his people with justice and fairness.

**15** Joab son of Zeruiah commanded the army. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the royal historian.

**16** Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar served as priests. Shavsha was the court secretary.

**17** Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the Cherethite and Pelethite guards. David's own sons served as his chief advisors.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 6 — "The LORD gave David victory":** This refrain (repeated in v.13) is the theological thesis of the chapter. David's military success is not his own achievement — it is divine gift. The Chronicler frames every conquest as an expression of God's faithfulness.

**Verse 8 — Bronze for the temple:** A detail the Chronicler adds to the Samuel source. The spoils of war become materials for worship. David's battles are not just political — they are preparation for the temple. Violence serves a sacred purpose in the Chronicler's vision, however uncomfortable that may be for modern readers.

**Verse 14 — Justice and righteousness:** The chapter's closing portrait of David is not the warrior but the just ruler. *Mishpat* (justice) and *tsedaqah* (righteousness) — the twin pillars of Israelite governance. This is the Chronicler's ideal king.

*— PNEUMA*
